text.p: Dickson Concepts (International) Ltd said on Monday it would pay US$78 million for all of the Class A voting shares of Barney's Inc, representing a 51 percent stake in the restructured U.S. retailer.

Dickson had reached an agreement in principle with Barney's and Barney's creditors to transfer the business, assets and certain of the liabilities of Barney's to a new company to be set up, referred to as new Barney's, Dickson said in a statement.

Dickson would also buy a 14.25 percent five-year senior subordinated convertible debenture for US$52 million from the restructured company and help arrange a US$75 million debt facility for the new Barney's, it said.
The remaining 49 percent of the new Barney's would be designated as Class B shares with limited voting rights and would be distributed under Barney's plan of reorganisation.
Dickson estimated the class A and B shares in new Barney's together at an aggregated amount of about US$153 million, Dickson Poon, chairman of Dickson, told a news conference.
The company's total outlay will be US$130 million, he said.

"The total outlay from Dickson Concept's point of view, at this moment, would be the US$78 million for the 51 percent plus the US$52 million for the convertible debenture, amounting to a total of US$130 million," he said.
If the convertible debenture is fully converted at a later stage Dickson then has the opportunity to increase its stake in the new Barney's to approximately 70 percent, Poon said.

Under the agreement, the minimum royalties payable under a restructured licence agreement with Isetan Co Ltd to cover Asia would go to a licensing royalty note with the principal amount of US$42 million, the statement said.
"This is to create a structure which would enable the minimum royalty that was under dispute to be assigned directly to the creditors," Poon said.

Dickson said any excess royalities payable under the restructured licence agreements together with payments to be made under the any new licence agreements would accrue for the benefit of new Barney's.
The agreement also contained provisions for the new Barney's to seek a listing of its common stock as soon as practicable, the statement said.

Poon declined to comment on the business of Barney's and said it was premature at this stage to discuss Dickson's plans for Barney's since the agreement has just been reached in principle and there was still additional work to be done.
The chairman also said Dickson had sufficient cash reserves and banking facilities available to satisfy its obligaions under the agreement.
"Moreover, should the acquisition be completed, the group would still be in a strong net cash position to take advantage of any other suitable investment opportunities which might arise," Poon said.
Dickson currently has HK$1.3 billion cash on hand and its cash position changes and is on the rise every day, he added.
Dickson would update its due diligence investigation of Barney's business and a definitive agreement would be finalised no later than August 15.
Should the acquisition proceed in accordance with the terms of the agreement it would take a minimum of five months to be completed.
